The problems started at check-in. The receptionist was cold and unfriendly, which I initially put down to it being late. However, things only got worse.

I was allocated an accessible room on the first floor, despite never requesting one. It was old, dated and had two separate single beds instead of a double bed. After speaking to the manager, I was moved the following day to a room on the fifth floor, which matched the standard my friends had received from the start. This meant I spent two of my four nights in an inferior room and only received the room I had paid for after complaining.

One incident involved a manager shouting at my friend for taking food to the beach, despite another member of staff having specifically told us this was allowed. The buffet food was repetitive and largely catered towards Russian guests, with some Turkish dishes. As a British guest, I found the options limited. The entertainment also appeared to be aimed almost entirely at Russian-speaking guests, making it difficult to feel included.

I appreciate that hotels cater to different nationalities, but I wish this had been made clearer before booking, as I expected a more international atmosphere.

Overall, my biggest disappointment was having to complain simply to receive the room I had paid for. Guests booking the same room category should receive rooms of an equal standard from the outset, and all guests should be treated with the same level of courtesy and respect.

The condition of the shower itself (files 1000104782.jpg and 1000104781.jpg) also raises serious hygiene concerns; it appears neglected and worn. We recently stayed at this hotel and unfortunately left with mixed feelings about our experience.

Firstly, I want to recognise the staff, particularly the guest relations team, who were exceptional throughout our stay. They were friendly, professional, highly capable, and resolved any issues we raised promptly and with genuine care. The front desk staff also deserve praise for being available at all hours and helping us order essential items to our room during the early hours of the morning, which was greatly appreciated.

However, despite the excellent service from the employees, our overall experience was significantly affected by the atmosphere created by some of the other guests. My wife wears a hijab, and as a mixed-race Muslim couple, we unfortunately received frequent stares throughout our stay. This was especially noticeable during dinner and while trying to enjoy the evening entertainment, where it often felt as though my wife’s hijab attracted unwanted attention from other patrons. It made us feel uncomfortable and, regrettably, unwelcome. People would turn and stare as my wife walked past and not smile or break their stare, as we ate people would stare and on one occasion someone muttered something while staring at her and moved their head side to side so as to imply we are from a certain background (they were wrong).

Because of this, we found ourselves spending as much time as possible away from the hotel each day and only returning when necessary, rather than enjoying the facilities we had paid for. I want to stress that the hotel staff themselves were welcoming, respectful, and kind, and they do not reflect the attitudes we experienced from some fellow guests. Equally, I understand that management cannot control the behaviour or prejudices of individual patrons. Nevertheless, the impact on our holiday was very real.

Another disappointment was a tour that we booked through the hotel. Unfortunately, the experience was poor, and we were left to make our own way back, resulting in an additional £40 Uber fare. To the hotel’s credit, the staff apologised sincerely and refunded the cost, which we appreciated, but the incident still dampened what should have been an enjoyable part of our trip.

In summary, the service provided by the hotel’s employees was excellent, particularly guest relations and reception, and they did everything within their power to assist us. Sadly, our comfort and enjoyment were overshadowed by the reactions and behaviour of other guests, which made us feel that we did not truly belong. We hope future visitors from all backgrounds and faiths can experience the same warmth from fellow patrons that the staff themselves so clearly demonstrated.

As it stands I cannot with a clean heart recommend this to any sisters who wear hijab and of colour.

There are numerous establishments along the promenade and in the surrounding area, so if you get bored, you'll always find something to do.

Regarding the rooms: I stayed in a sea-view room, and it speaks for itself; just look at the photo. Don't worry about the road—you won't hear loud music or roaring engines; the traffic is very calm and quiet.

This year, the beach area is located directly across from the hotel, which is a great plus. The beach itself is very clean; you won't find any trash, food scraps, or cigarette butts. Waiters regularly come by to offer drinks and fruit.

I have no complaints about the food in the main restaurant: everything was delicious, both visually and flavorfully. I don't recall ever liking the cheese or cold meats at other hotels. During my stay, I tried salmon, dorado, shrimp, crayfish, lamb, and beef. You could eat all kinds of meat in one meal, and I guarantee you'll be satisfied.

A word about alcohol. The hotel offers both Turkish and imported drinks. Regarding imported drinks:
Ballantine's, Jameson, Black Label, Chivas Regal 12 whiskey, and a few others—I haven't even had a chance to try them all; there's Campari, two types of gin—Gordon's and Beefeater. Jägermeister deserves a special mention—I haven't found it in any other hotel at this price.

The hotel staff is a true testament to this hotel. The entertainment staff is unobtrusive and doesn't make you want to run away. Despite this, and the fact that I'm a 35-year-old man, I went to aqua aerobics and morning exercises, which helped me stay in shape all these days.

The waiters in the restaurant and bar are all very friendly and diligent. It was never a problem to be sitting at a dirty table, missing an ashtray, or having an empty glass. They always greet you with a smile (especially Naz). Say hello to Elizaveta; it was very unexpected to meet a Russian girl.

I could write about each employee individually, but that would be too much text.

To the management of the Megasaray Hotel: value your employees – they are the jewel of your hotel, and they are the ones who make your guests' stay unforgettable.

Updating the score as the hotel appears to take feedback seriously and is keen to fix, update based on customer feedback.

I booked primarily on the huge amount of positive reviews but I simply do not get it and I must have missed something as it was lacking in areas.  The all inclusives in Lara, Belek were much better.

For context, I have stayed at over 10 different hotels across the Antalya area and Megasaray simply does not compete.  This is, thus far, my least favoured hotel that  I have stayed at in the region.

Positives
Some of the food items are a slightly better taste-wise than other Antalya all inclusive hotels we have stayed at.  However, overall the food is distinctly mediocre with the desserts unfortunately tasting the worst of any of the all inclusive hotels I have stayed at.  That being said, when they made fresh live Kunefe, it was great but that happened once in our 8 day stay.

The staff interactions were positive, I felt like they were attentive and listened.  We found them to be polite and helpful throughout.

The massages in the spa were good and the team there were nice, friendly and helpful rather than being pushy for sales.

Negatives

No Air Con
In April (presuming many other months too) the AC controls in the room do not work! It will not cool the room at all.  You are left sweating in a room unless you keep the windows/ balcony doors open.  Don’t think you will get much sleep doing this as the noise from the road and cars will keep you up, if not the heat will get you.  Also opening the balcony door to survive the room temp means random bugs in your room. Such a terrible system to which prioritises their cost savings over your comfort.

After complaints about this, they will offer you a noisy broken fan to use in the room.  If I knew this would be the case at this hotel, I would not have booked to stay here.  I have not had this issue at any other Antalya hotel I stayed at.  You will not get a comfortable night sleep here!

Dated compact rooms
The rooms are compact with small bathrooms and furniture making manoeuvring around the room cumbersome.

At a similar price point, you get more comfortable and spacious rooms. A balcony that just about allows you to lean (more a Juliet balcony than anything with purpose).

The rooms are worn in many areas and showing their signs of need a refurb.

The rooms are not compatible for those with mobility issues or disabled.

No reading lights by the bed, choice of bright lights or no lights! Fix up your room design!

TV is never a major concern but don’t expect any recognisable English channels, not even BBC News or CNN is available.  The TV is not a smart tv either so best just to watch things on your own devices.

Main restaurant
If you come at a busy time which is most of the time, the chairs and tables are too closely packed together in that you will get bumped/pushed by people simply trying to get by.  Limited bench seating and it is always crowded and taken.  Food overall is ok but the desserts need sorting out, as none of them were in the slightest bit nice.

Indoor facilities
The gym is in the basement with no wifi coverage and very feint phone signal so if you want to stream music during workout, you are out of luck.  To access the gym you have to walk pass the indoor pool and sauna.  The gym floor was slippery indicating people would just pop in after swimming.  The gym is unattended with no functional AC means it gets very hot.  The machinery is dated, patch repaired in many instances although water bottles are freely available and you will usually find towels.  It was barely used by people when I was there which was a plus for me.

The sauna, steam room and hammam were all accessible and working when we were there but the atmosphere isn’t a serene one.  It isn’t a tranquil place to relax.  The loungers there are stained and worn.

We ended our stay at this hotel with very mixed feelings.

The positives first:

Location & View: The location is simply phenomenal. The view of the sea is exactly what you imagine a dream vacation to be.

Service: A big compliment to the entire team. The friendliness and helpfulness of the staff are outstanding and ensure that you feel well taken care of despite the shortcomings.

Culinary: For an all-inclusive concept, the food is of a very high standard. It is varied, fresh, and truly delicious – there is absolutely nothing to criticize here.

The decisive drawback – The Rooms:
As positive as the rest of the hotel is, the condition of our room was disappointing. To say that the building is "showing its age" would be an understatement. The furnishings are massively worn, the furniture looks damaged, and the entire ambiance is far from what is internationally understood as a 5-star standard.

It's truly a shame to see that no investment has been made here for a long time. In this price range, a well-maintained, contemporary interior isn't a bonus, but a basic requirement. I've rarely experienced such a glaring discrepancy between the quality of the staff and the poor condition of the building.

In conclusion: If you can overlook a worn-out room, you'll have a good time here thanks to the location and the great team. However, if you're looking for true 5-star luxury, you should wait until the urgently needed renovations have been completed.
